text: Sessions Insight 是 DSH Web 的会话洞察与管理插件，随 Cyrus Plugins 集合安装。它在侧边栏提供会话面板，从 Claude Code、DSH 和 Codex 读取会话，并展示轮次上下文、工具调用、压缩点、用量和成本。用户可以跨项目浏览与搜索记录、重命名和分组会话、确认后删除，也可生成交接简报并创建新 DSH 会话。余额与版本查询为可选设置；余额功能使用 DeepSeek 凭据或已登录账号。

Sessions Insight adds a DSH Web sidebar for browsing Claude Code, DSH, and Codex sessions. It shows turn context, tools, compactions, usage, and cost; users can search transcripts, rename and group sessions, confirm deletion, and hand work to a new DSH session.
我想在一个界面里查看 DSH、Codex 和 Claude Code 的历史会话。
能不能按项目目录把不同会话整理出来？
我想知道某一轮对话用了多少上下文、调用了哪些工具。
帮我从以前的会话记录里搜一句话或某个工具调用。
我需要给一批会话改名、分组，或者清理不再需要的记录。
想把当前工作的背景整理成简报，交给一个新的 DSH 会话继续做。
有没有办法根据一段会话自动生成简短标题？
I need to find an old coding session by searching its transcript or tool inputs.
Can I compare token usage, compactions, and tool activity across earlier conversations?
I want to group and rename several saved sessions without editing their log files.
Sessions Insight 的功能「跨来源会话浏览」：侧边栏按工作目录汇总 Claude Code、DSH 与 Codex 会话，选择项目、会话和轮次查看详情。
Sessions Insight 的功能「轮次上下文洞察」：查看各轮上下文归因、峰值、用量、工具调用、压缩次数、技能证据和耗时。
Sessions Insight 的功能「会话成本估算」：依据各轮模型用量和内置价格表计算费用，并按价格表与币种分组呈现。
Sessions Insight 的功能「会话全文搜索」：快速层检索标题、首条输入和工作目录，深度层扫描会话正文并显示覆盖情况。
Sessions Insight 的功能「会话管理」：批量选择会话、手动或 AI 改名、分组筛选和移动，并支持确认后删除记录。
Sessions Insight 的功能「会话交接」：从现有记录提取工作简报，创建或复用工作区并投递给新 DSH 会话。
Sessions Insight 的功能「余额与版本工具」：用户可选择启用 DeepSeek 余额展示和 npm 版本检查，相关查询也可手动触发。
Sessions Insight 的功能「AI 会话命名」：把会话最早的用户输入整理后交给 DSH 当前模型，生成并校验一个简短标题。
Sessions Insight 使用前须知：余额查询默认关闭；启用后会请求 api.deepseek.com，并使用 DSH 配置的 DeepSeek 凭据或登录账号。
Sessions Insight 使用前须知：版本查询仅在启用或手动触发时访问 registry.npmjs.org。

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Cyrus Plugins · @cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins：A plugin collection for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Install this one bundle to get every plugin listed below; each plugin can also be installed on its own.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Install：Requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 or newer (see `docs/adr/0002-asar-021-is-the-contract.md`). First decide which profile to install into: the desktop app uses `desktop`, `dsh web` on the command line uses `web`. Installing into the wrong profile does not error; the plugin just never shows up.

**Install the collection (recommended)** to get every plugin at once; when a plugin is added to the collection later, upgrading the collection brings it in.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins   # desktop app
dsh plugin --profile web     add @cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins   # dsh web
```

**Install a single plugin**:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @cyrusdoyle/dsh-sessions-insight   # desktop app
dsh plugin --profile web     add @cyrusdoyle/dsh-sessions-insight   # dsh web
```

Then **fully quit and reopen** DSH. "Cyrus Plugins" or "Sessions Insight" in the plugin manager means it worked.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Install：**Installing from this working tree (developing the collection)**: the desktop plugin manager's "Add plugin" also accepts a local directory — point it at this checkout's absolute path. DSH records it as `"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins": "link:<that path>"`: a symlink into your working tree, not a copy, and nothing is built for you. The host resolves `lib/index.js` through that link, and `lib/` is gitignored, so build it first (the collection embeds the compiled stylesheet, so the CSS step comes first):

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Install：```bash
node scripts/build-css.mjs plugins/sessions-insight && npx tsdown --minify
```

Then fully quit and reopen DSH. Later edits only need a rebuild and a restart — there is no need to reinstall.

Each plugin's usage, permission boundary and known limitations live in its own README.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Settings, balance and update checks：The collection embeds the same plugin source as the standalone member (ADR 0009), so its runtime behaviour is the Sessions Insight behaviour: read-only insight, the handoff, confirmed session deletion, plus a settings page and two opt-in utilities.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Settings, balance and update checks：- **Settings are saved by the Host.** `/api/dsh-sessions-insight/settings` is read-only; the six switches (session overview, Skills tab, cumulative level chart, expand tools by default, balance display, automatic version checks) are written through the Host's configuration form and stored by the Host. The plugin writes no config file.
- **Balance and version checks are off by default.** Turning one on — or pressing its button — is the only thing that makes the plugin call out. Outbound traffic is limited to two fixed HTTPS endpoints, `https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` and `https://registry.npmjs.org/@cyrusdoyle%2F.../latest`, with no redirects, no cookies and no caller-controlled URL.
- **Credentials**: the balance check resolves the credential reference configured for the DeepSeek official adapter (`apiKeyEnv`, default `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`), then falls back to the signed-in DeepSeek account. Custom provider references are not followed; the plugin never stores or logs the key.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Settings, balance and update checks：The plugin README has the full route list, defaults and known limitations.
@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Repository layout：This is a pnpm monorepo. Only the collection and `plugins/*` are published; the rest is inlined into the plugins at build time.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Repository layout：| Path                         | Contents                                                                  | Published                             |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `/` (root)                   | The collection bundle: `cordis.patch.yml`, `locale/`, its own `lib/`      | **yes**, `@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins`         |
| `plugins/sessions-insight`    | The Sessions Insight plugin: host half and browser half                       | **yes**, `@cyrusdoyle/dsh-sessions-insight` |
| `packages/session-contract`  | The unified IR, wire types and their guards                               | no                                    |
| `packages/session-readers`   | Claude Code / Codex / DSH readers                                         | no                                    |
| `packages/plugin-kit`        | Plugin-agnostic JSON envelope and URL spelling                            | no                                    |
| `packages/plugin-kit-host`   | Host-half plumbing: route table, same-origin gate, envelo

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Repository layout：Dependencies point one way only: `plugins/* → packages/*`. The package-name-to-source mapping lives in `tooling/aliases.ts`, and `tsconfig.json`'s `paths` mirrors it, so tests, the preview app and the build never need the internal packages built first.

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Development：```bash
pnpm install
```

```bash
pnpm dev
```

The preview runs at <http://localhost:5178> and reads your real local sessions; add `?theme=light` or `?theme=dark` to switch themes.

Run the gates before you commit:

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.client.json && npx vitest run && node scripts/build-css.mjs plugins/sessions-insight && npx tsdown --minify && node scripts/check-bundle.mjs plugins/sessions-insight && node scripts/check-bundle.mjs .
```

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Development：CI runs the same gates and additionally fails when the committed `plugins/sessions-insight/lib/` differs from a rebuild — see [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](./.github/workflows/ci.yml).

Rebuild the artifacts and check that the profile's link really points at your build (this does not install — installation happens in the DSH plugin manager):

```bash
pnpm install:plugin
```

@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Development：Regenerate the README screenshots from the preview (headless Chrome, 1440×900; add `-- --theme light` for the light theme). They show the sessions on your machine, so look at them before committing:

```bash
pnpm screenshots
```

Optional browser checks (need a local Chrome; not part of CI):

- `pnpm smoke:preview` measures the mounted panel in both themes under `?probe=1`.
- `pnpm check:ui` drives the session-menu interactions against a fixture server.
@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugins README · Publishing：Follow [`docs/RELEASE.md`](./docs/RELEASE.md): the member and the collection share one version number and are published together, member first (ADR 0010).
